title: N.L. families to receive $500 per child before the end of the year

image.caption: N.L. Finance Minister Craig Pardy and Premier Tony Wakeham announced families will recieve $500 per child in the province's latest affordability benefit. (Terry Roberts/CBC)

blocks.text: Families in Newfoundland and Labrador who receive the Canada Child Benefit will receive $500 per child under the age of 18 as part of the province’s latest affordability measure connected to skyrocketing oil revenues.
Announcement is province's latest affordability measure connected to high oil revenues

Families in Newfoundland and Labrador who receive the Canada Child Benefit will get a one-time $500 payment per child as part of the province’s latest affordability measure connected to skyrocketing oil revenues.
At an announcement Monday morning, Premier Tony Wakeham said families will receive a tax-free payment for children under the age of 18.
The top-up will cost the province $36 million, and Wakeham said it will help about 46,500 families and 77,000 children across the province.
“That is money back in people's pockets,” said Wakeham.

For families where the parents aren’t in the same household, Finance Minister Craig Pardy said the funds will go to whichever parent is receiving the Canada Child Benefit. He also said parents will receive it by the end of the year.
Pardy said the amount was determined by looking at projected oil revenues.
The government has announced other affordability measures in the last few months, including $100 to $500 payments to seniors making $100,000 or less annually.

In September, Pardy announced high oil prices have boosted Newfoundland and Labrador’s revenue, and that 80 per cent of the extra revenues will be used against the province’s debt, while 20 percent will be used for affordability measures.
Pardy told reporters that as long as the province continues to collect the higher than usual oil revenues, people can expect more affordability measure announcements.
“I think we'll respond to affordability as best we [can] and I can probably envision another,” he said.
